title: Washington Is About to Make the Energy Crisis a Whole Lot Worse
author: Murtaza Hussain
content:
Eight months into the US-Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz is still contested--
and the oil shock nearly everyone predicted never arrived.

Gregory Brew, senior energy analyst at Eurasia Group and a historian of modern
Iran, explains why crude sits in the $90-$110 band instead of $250:
alternative pipeline routes, high global inventories, a steep cut in Chinese
imports, and an oil market practiced at absorbing shocks. He also breaks down
the US escort operation moving 9 to 10 million barrels a day through the
strait--supertankers running dark through the Omani channel--and why he calls
it a Band-Aid.  
  
Also: the attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, Iranian production down
to 2 million barrels a day, record US diesel prices ahead of the midterms, and
why Brew expects Tehran to escalate rather than capitulate.
